title: Dedicated capacity intake heuristic and stakeholder synthesis
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Consolidate a deterministic intake heuristic for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that maps customer workloads to SLA targets, reserved throughput, GPU family recommendations, and scaling policy templates. Goal is to reduce sales/solutions handoff time, surface clear trade-offs to customers, and create a predictable internal routing for Dedicated pool sizing and SLA negotiation.

Background: We frequently receive enterprise requests with incomplete signals: vague RPS, token distribution unknown, burst tolerance ambiguous, and regulatory constraints that affect Private vs Hosted choices. This ticket gathers stakeholder inputs (Sales, Solutions, Infra Eng, Runtime, Security) and produces a single-page intake heuristic + scoring rubric that can be used by Solutions/Sales and the Capacity Concierge to fast-track decisions or escalate to a custom architecture.

Scope: Produce the heuristic and a small decision tree (textual) that covers: SLA latency bands (sub-50ms, 50-150ms, 150-400ms), throughput/commit levels (tokens/sec or requests/sec), GPU family mapping (A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100, L4-32GB equivalent for embeddings), sustained vs burst capacity, autoscaling guardrails (min/max pool size, cooldowns), and fallback policy recommendations (model downgrades, cross-region routing). Include example mappings for three canonical workload archetypes: low-latency conversational (LLM-chat), high-throughput embedding indexer, and mixed inference (reranking + generation).

Non-goals: This ticket does not modify runtime code or autoscaler implementation. It focuses on the intake rubric and stakeholder alignment; follow-up tickets will implement automation or UI changes in Console and Intake forms.
acceptance_criteria: A clear intake rubric document exists (Confluence link) that maps customer input fields to recommended SLA bands and GPU families
A scoring rubric (0-100) that yields a recommended 'capacity band' (Small/Medium/Large/Enterprise) with rationale examples
Stakeholder sign-off: Solutions, Sales, Runtime Eng, Capacity Ops, and Security have provided written feedback or approval
Three customer archetype worked examples included (chat, embeddings, mixed) with estimated reserved throughput and recommended scaling policy
A short follow-up backlog with prioritized implementation tasks for Console intake, Capacity Concierge automation, and runbook updates
comments: 2026-02-25 Priya K: Created ticket after Wednesday sales sync; recurring delays when Sales asks for 'an estimate' without clear signals. Goal: reduce back-and-forth and speed up time-to-proposal.

2026-02-28 Diego M: Drafted initial scoring factors (latency requirement, QPS, average tokens per request, burst multiplier, data-sensitivity). Shared with Runtime Eng for kernel / GPU mapping feedback.

2026-03-02 Anika Bose (Runtime): Recommended that sub-50ms targets should default to H100-backed pools where available; add note about sequence length >2048 impacting kernel choice and effective throughput.

2026-03-03 Luis R (Capacity Ops): Raised operational constraint: reserved pools with <2 nodes of H100 are fragile for maintenance; recommend minimum pool size and explicit maintenance windows for Enterprise band.
2026-03-05 Legal/Security: Confirmed that customers requiring 'air-gapped' must use Private deployment; intake should flag KMS/HSM requirements and add 3-week lead time.

2026-03-07 Solutions feedback: Need a 'quick propose' column in rubric with a conservative estimate for response time to customer (under NDA) — proposed template attached as Drive doc: https://drive.redwood/example/dedicated-quick-propose

2026-03-10 Diego M: Incorporated feedback and produced canonical mapping table. Pushed draft to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/dedicated/intake-heuristic. Requested runtime validation on throughput numbers for each GPU family.

2026-03-12 Runtime Eng review: Performed bench runs on perf-lab; attached perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/bench/dedicated-gpu-mapping. Observations: A100-40GB performs well for short-sequence embeddings but suffers with long contexts (>4k). Added margin multipliers to the scoring rubric.

2026-03-14 Priya K: Held stakeholder review (Solutions, Sales, Runtime, Capacity Ops). Collected final edits; next steps: convert rubric into a JSON schema for Console intake (follow-up ticket) and draft Capacity Concierge playbook.
